button.$description: Button component tokens. These sit above semantic tokens — consume these in button CSS, not semantic tokens directly.

font-weight.$description: Button label weight — medium across all sizes

gap.$description: Gap between icon and label inside a button

border-width.$description: Border width for secondary and ghost variants

required-gap.$description: Inline gap before a required marker

gap.$description: Gap between input and hint text

stack-gap.$description: Vertical gap between stacked fields in a form

max-width.$description: Maximum width for standard page content

compact-max-width.$description: Maximum width for compact page content

max-width.$description: Maximum width for a focused, single-column form composition

size.$description: Clipped dimension for visually hidden accessible text

offset.$description: Clipped offset for visually hidden accessible text

link-underline-offset.$description: Readable underline offset for inline links

code-relative-size.$description: Relative size for inline and block code

color.$description: Primitive color scale. 25 steps per hue (0–1000). Step N has L = N/1000 in OKLCH — perceptually uniform across all hues at the same step. Chroma (C) tapers at extremes to stay within sRGB gamut. Hex values are approximate sRGB-gamut-mapped fallbacks; verify with culori or oklch.com before production. OKLCH values are authoritative. Do not use these directly in components — reference semantic tokens instead.

50.$description: Off-white — page background in light mode

75.$description: Subtle divider, input border on white

800.$description: Primary text on light — near max contrast

neutral.$description: Achromatic neutral. C=0 throughout — use for text, surfaces, borders, dividers, shadows.

50.$description: Faint blue — info surface, selected bg

450.$description: Primary action blue — use for action.primary.bg

blue.$description: Blue-indigo hue (H=250). Primary action family. Peak chroma at step 450–500.

450.$description: Error base — use for destructive actions

red.$description: Red-orange hue (H=22). Destructive action and error family. Peak chroma at step 450–500.

green.$description: Emerald-green hue (H=150). Success family. Peak chroma at step 450–500.

amber.$description: Amber-yellow hue (H=75). Warning family. Peak chroma at step 350–400 (yellow-amber peaks at higher L than other hues).

shadow.$description: Elevation shadow scale. Shadow color uses neutral with alpha; do not hardcode.

4.$description: 4px — base grid unit, minimum meaningful gap

6.$description: 6px — tight list gap, badge padding, icon-to-label gap

8.$description: 8px — compact gap, small inset, dense list item

12.$description: 12px — control inner padding y, tight section gap

16.$description: 16px — base component padding, form field gap

20.$description: 20px — stacked field gap, relaxed list gap

space.$description: Spacing scale. Token name = pixel value (space.16 = 16px). Micro tier (1–3) for optical nudges and fine adjustments; grid tier (4+) for layout. Compiled to rem for layout/typography output via SD4 transform. Negative offsets are not in the scale — use calc(-1 * var(--ds-space-N)) at the call site, or define a named component token for recurring structural offsets (e.g., card bleed).

size.$description: Type size scale. These are raw values — reference semantic type tokens in components.

z.$description: Z-index scale. Use only these values — never arbitrary z-index integers.

raised.$description: Slightly elevated in-flow elements (sticky headers within a section)

dropdown.$description: Dropdowns, menus, popovers anchored to trigger

action.$description: Action semantic tokens — buttons, links, interactive controls. Mode-aware: swap these per data-mode. Every variant carries rest, hover, active, and disabled, because a system without roles for the interaction states gives an adopted system's hover colour nowhere to map.

bg-hover.$description: Primary action background under pointer or keyboard focus

bg-active.$description: Primary action background while being pressed

bg-disabled.$description: Primary action background when the action is unavailable

bg.$description: Secondary button background — typically transparent or very light
Ghost button background — transparent at rest

default.$description: Default divider and outline — cards, input borders, table dividers

strong.$description: Stronger border — active input ring, emphasized dividers

subtle.$description: Very light separator — inner table rules, inline sections

focus.$description: Focus ring color — applied to all interactive elements

action.$description: Border on secondary/ghost buttons in their action color

danger.$description: Input or control in error state

success.$description: Input or control in valid/success state

elevation.$description: Elevation semantic tokens. These complete the surface roles: surface.raised and surface.overlay named the colour of a lifted plane without naming its shadow, so "raised" was only half-defined. Elevation is a real design concept that both design tools and production encode, and it needs a role of its own to survive a round trip.

raised.$description: Lifted just off the page — cards, panels. Pairs with surface.raised.

overlay.$description: Floating above the page — menus, popovers, dropdowns. Pairs with surface.overlay.

modal.$description: Above everything — dialogs and sheets that take focus from the page.

feedback.$description: Feedback state semantic tokens — alerts, banners, badges, form states.

focus.$description: Focus ring tokens. Applied to all interactive elements via :focus-visible. Must never be removed — only styled.

ring-offset-color.$description: Focus outline offset gap color — typically matches the surface behind the element

ring-offset.$description: Gap between element edge and focus ring

icon.$description: Icon semantic tokens. Separate from text because icon colour is routinely not text colour — an icon often needs more weight than the label beside it to read at the same size. Without these roles an adopted system's icon colours have to borrow a text role and stop being independently themeable.

default.$description: Default icon colour, paired with text.primary

muted.$description: De-emphasised icon — decorative, or paired with secondary text

on-action.$description: Icon sitting on an action surface, paired with text.on-action

accent.$description: Icon carrying the accent colour, such as a leading icon in a link

palette.$description: Named scheme and mode palettes. CSS remaps public semantic roles to these tokens; raw color values never live in component or composition styles.

surface.$description: Surface semantic tokens. These define what backgrounds exist in the system. Always use these — never raw color scale values.

base.$description: Primary content surface — cards, panels, the main content area

sunken.$description: Recessed input areas, code blocks, inset sections

hover.$description: Hover state for interactive list items, menu items

text.$description: Text color semantic tokens. All text in the system must use one of these roles.

primary.$description: Primary body and heading text — highest contrast

inverse.$description: Text on dark/filled surfaces — e.g., primary button label

on-action.$description: Text sitting on an action-primary surface (button label)

type.$description:
Typographic semantic roles. Before these, the entire semantic layer was colour: text.* named what a string means politically (primary, muted, danger) but nothing named what it means typographically. Type is half of any design system, and text styles are first-class objects in design tools — a vocabulary that cannot say "this is body text" cannot round-trip them.

Each role is a composite: family, size, weight, and line height together, because that is the unit a designer actually chooses and the unit a design tool actually stores.

display.$description: Largest type. Marketing headers and empty-state hero text; rarely more than once per screen.

sm.$description: Smallest heading — group labels within a section.

lg.$description: Lead paragraph, or body text in a reading-first layout.

md.$description: Default body text. The role everything else is judged against.

sm.$description: Secondary body text — helper copy, dense tables.

label.$description: Form labels and control text. Heavier than body at the same size so it reads as interface rather than prose.

caption.$description: Smallest supporting text — timestamps, field hints, footnotes.
